_comment: The AGENT-ERROR MARKER: how a provider-side failure (an API error, an
out-of-credits refusal, a model overload) is spelled inside a session's
conversation, and what a reader must extract from it.
There is no structured error field on the wire. claudemon's managed-update
fold (services/claudemon/src/providers/mod.rs, AgentUpdate::Error) turns a
provider error into an ORDINARY assistant text turn prefixed with the
marker below, deliberately: the renderer only renders known item kinds and
would have dropped a bespoke variant. That makes the prefix a real
cross-process contract — the Rust side writes it, the desktop's
workerFailure.ts reads it to tell a worker that DIED from one that
FINISHED, and a manager that cannot tell those apart records a crash as a
landed outcome (observed 2026-08-21: an out-of-credits worker woke its
manager as 'Worker finished' with the error string as its summary).
The NON-failure cases are the load-bearing half. A reader that fired on
prose merely mentioning an error, or on a marker that trails rather than
leads, would relabel successful work as a crash — a new bug worse than the
one this closes, so the shapes we must NOT match are pinned too.
THE BLOCK REGISTRY. Every array-of-objects block in this file must be
declared here and everything here must be a block — closure in both
directions. Held by cmd/brain/corpusvocab_test.go and
apps/desktop/src/main/services/contractsVocabulary.test.ts.

cases.why: One worker final message, and whether a reader must call it a failure — plus, when it is one, the exact reason text the reader must extract.

cases.name: out of credits (the live 2026-08-21 case)
cases.finalMessage: ⚠️ Error: Credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API.
cases.reason: Credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API.
cases.why: The exact shape that woke a Fleet Manager as 'Worker finished' with an API refusal as the worker's summary.

cases.name: model overload
cases.why: A transient provider failure — retryable, so the manager must see it as an open dispatch rather than a landed one.

cases.name: marker with surrounding whitespace still counts
cases.why: The conversation turn may arrive padded; leading whitespace must not hide the marker from the reader.

cases.name: multi-line error keeps only its first line as the reason
cases.finalMessage:
⚠️ Error: request failed
stack trace line 1
stack trace line 2
cases.why: The reason rides a wake BULLET, whose grammar is one line per entry — a stack trace would break the parser, not just the formatting.

cases.name: bare marker with no message
cases.reason: the provider reported an error with no message
cases.why: An empty reason must still read as a failure; a blank tail would render as a bullet that says nothing happened.

cases.name: an ordinary successful report is NOT a failure
cases.finalMessage: All 42 tests pass. Committed as abc1234.
cases.why: The common case. A reader that flagged this would relabel every landed dispatch as a crash.

cases.name: prose that merely MENTIONS an error is not a failure
cases.finalMessage: I hit an error in the parser and fixed it. ⚠️ Error handling is now covered.
cases.why: Worker reports discuss errors constantly; the marker is a leading prefix, never a substring match.

cases.name: the marker must lead the message, not trail it
cases.finalMessage:
Here is what happened:
⚠️ Error: something broke
cases.why: The fold only ever emits the marker as the WHOLE turn, so a marker mid-message is the worker quoting one, not the daemon reporting one.

cases.name: empty final message is not a failure signal
cases.why: A worker that produced no text is silent, not failed — its emptiness is already handled by the wake's own no-task and genuine-idle gates.

cases.name: an error turn the store coalesced with the reply that followed it
cases.finalMessage:
⚠️ Error: workspacer MCP server(s) did not attach to this Copilot session: workspacer.
OK, I created the file.
cases.reason: workspacer MCP server(s) did not attach to this Copilot session: workspacer.
cases.why: claudemon's conversation store merges consecutive assistant_text items, so a mid-turn error and the turn's real reply arrive as ONE message. Observed live on a copilot session whose facade could not attach. The writer now ends the error with a newline (providers/mod.rs) and the reader must take only the first line — without both halves the reason read '...attach: workspacer.OK, I created the file.'
